overview: This file contains a January 1937 despatch from American Consul Edward S. Maney transmitting English translations of Taiwan’s original 1933 foreign-exchange-control regulations and their December 1936 amendments. The enclosed orders reveal the extensive system developed by Taiwan’s Japanese colonial Government General to control gold exports, currency and exchange transactions, remittances, letters of credit, negotiable instruments, foreign borrowing, export proceeds, and the activities of banks and money changers. They also prescribe detailed applications, monthly statements, transaction reports, and procedures involving the Governor General, Customs, post offices, and the Bank of Taiwan.

people.name: Chuhei Matsuo
people.role: Interpreter at the American Consulate in Taihoku

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting Taiwan foreign-exchange regulations and amendments
subfiles.about: The American consul transmits the original and amended Taiwanese foreign-exchange-control orders with translations prepared by Chuhei Matsuo.
subfiles.summary: Maney transmits Taiwan's 1933 foreign-exchange orders and 1936 amendments, separately enacted from Japan's own currency statutes.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Government General Order No. 97 amending foreign-exchange controls
subfiles.from: Seizo Kobayashi, Governor General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Order No. 97 substantially expands and revises Taiwan’s regulations governing foreign exchange, gold, negotiable instruments, remittances, exports, and exchange businesses.
subfiles.summary: The order amends the 1933 foreign-exchange regulations by requiring reports on gold exports, prohibiting speculative exchange transactions, and revising exemptions and monetary thresholds for travel, family support, and other remittances. It imposes detailed controls on letters of credit, the import and export of negotiable instruments, exports made without foreign drafts, and the recovery of overseas proceeds. It also establishes licensing and reporting requirements for foreign-exchange banks and money exchange merchants and strengthens the Governor General’s authority to demand or waive reports.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Government General Order No. 98 amending enforcement regulations
subfiles.from: Seizo Kobayashi, Governor General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Order No. 98 revises the procedural rules and application requirements used to enforce Taiwan’s amended foreign-exchange controls.
subfiles.summary: This order amends the enforcement regulations accompanying the foreign-exchange-control regime. It specifies information required in applications concerning delayed or waived collection of export proceeds, foreign-currency securities, and authorization to conduct foreign-exchange business. It also prescribes reports for banks and money exchange merchants, routes many filings through the Bank of Taiwan, and revises procedures for stamping imported foreign-currency negotiable instruments.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Government General Order No. 57 establishing foreign-exchange controls
subfiles.from: Kenzo Nakagawa, Governor General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Order No. 57 establishes the principal regulations governing foreign exchange in colonial Taiwan, effective May 1, 1933.
subfiles.summary: The order restricts gold exports, speculative currency dealings, foreign remittances, foreign-currency securities, foreign loans, letters of credit, and the import or export of negotiable instruments without official permission. It regulates exports made without drafts and requires the repatriation of many overseas proceeds, while defining privileges and reporting obligations for designated foreign-exchange banks. Further provisions mandate reports on a broad range of foreign-currency transactions and holdings, authorize official inspections and compulsory disposition of certain assets, and coordinate the new regime with earlier capital-flight-prevention orders.

subfiles.title: Taiwan Government General Order No. 60 enforcing foreign-exchange controls
subfiles.from: Kenzo Nakagawa, Governor General of Taiwan
subfiles.about: Order No. 60 prescribes the application forms and administrative procedures for permissions and reports required under Order No. 57.
subfiles.summary: The enforcement order requires most applications to be submitted in duplicate through the Bank of Taiwan and specifies the information needed for each category of controlled transaction. Its provisions cover gold exports, currency and bill transactions, remittances, foreign-currency credits and contracts, borrowing, letters of credit, negotiable instruments, and exports without foreign drafts. It also sets procedures for overseas transactions, regulatory reports, and the official stamping of eligible foreign-currency negotiable instruments; translations of the separate forms themselves are omitted.

interest: Shows Taiwan's 1930s foreign-exchange controls, extending Japanese capital restrictions to travel funds, securities, and trade.
